about: Results of the AI editorial review for articles published with the automated label. Not a person's review.

entries.notes: Verified yum cha definition, regions, 食點心, 早茶/下午茶/飲夜茶, 嘆茶, the push-cart method, bill-card marking and tea etiquette (pour for others, 80% and the proverb, finger kowtow and Qianlong story, lid signal, dessert any time, declining carts, lazy Susan, chopsticks, insisting on paying, traditional bill reckoning) against the Yum cha wikitext; Four Heavenly Kings, spellings and haa1 gaau2 siu1 maai2 against Har gow; family-style three-or-four pieces, 燒賣 and 腸粉 descriptions against Dim sum; Jyutping for 蝦餃, 燒賣 siu1 maai6-2, 叉燒包, 腸粉 coeng4-2 fan2, 鳳爪, 點心 (四五籠 example), 斟茶 zam1 caa4, the 籠 classifier and 埋單 against Wiktionary. Recomputed 2 x 4 = 8. Changed: cut unsourced claims that 'dim sum' comes from the Cantonese pronunciation and covers cakes, and that 蝦餃 is also called 水晶蝦餃 with a flour wrapper (replaced with Wikipedia's wheat/tapioca starch and translucent-skin description and Wiktionary's senses of 點心); 'many restaurants now use' paper ordering changed to Wikipedia's 'other restaurants may'. Added six Wiktionary sources. App claims match catalog.

Verified every Jyutping reading and gloss against Wiktionary entries in wikt_log: 你好 nei5 hou2 (attention usage note), 早晨 zou2 san4 Cantonese 'good morning' with the 王小姐 example, 早敨 zou2 tau2 including the rude sense, 唔該 m4 goi1 three senses, examples and 'may be offensive' note, 多謝 do1 ze6 usage note, 對唔住, 唔好意思 (alt ji3 si3), 再見 polite, 拜拜 baai3-1 baai3 informal, phono-semantic match of bye-bye and Hong Kong euphemism 'to die', 得閒飲茶 under 飲茶; 唔 m4 negation and 唔好 negative imperative against Wikipedia Cantonese grammar. Changed: added Wiktionary's usage note that 你好嗎 is a literal translation not commonly used among native speakers (body and takeaway had presented it as the normal question); reworded an unsupported 'therefore' inference about 唔好意思; fixed the worked-example count (six moments use six distinct phrases, not five); 'a light sorry' replaced with the Wiktionary gloss; added eight Wiktionary sources the text cites. App claims match catalog.

Verified each classifier reading and use against Wiktionary (個 go3 incl. money; 隻 zek3 one of a pair, birds and certain animals, body parts, utensils, with 兩隻豬 and 一隻鞋/一雙鞋; 條 tiu4 incl. 一條毛, lives, Cantonese derogatory 嗰條女 and 三條九 = 999; 張 zoeng1 incl. 幾張凳, 兩張紙, Cantonese knives and ages 三張嘢; 本 bun2; 架 gaa3 incl. dialectal vehicles; 對 deoi3 兩對鞋; 啲 di1). Demonstrative + classifier rule, 呢/依 in fast speech, 嗰本書, 呢啲車, 佢本書 possession and 架車撻唔著 definiteness checked against Wikipedia Cantonese grammar; 張 vs 條 for 櫈 in Cantonese, Yue 隻 for people, 我本書 and classifier variability against Chinese classifier. Changed: 'many animals' to 'certain animals' per Wiktionary; corrected the worked-example summary (the plural swaps 本 for 啲, so it is not true that only the word in front changes); added six Wiktionary sources cited in the text. App claims match catalog.

Verified 0-10, 100, 1,000, 萬 maan6 and 億 jik1 Jyutping against the Chinese numerals comparison table; 兩 before a classifier, 廿 jaa6 / 卅 saa1-aa6 / 卌 sei3-aa6 / 呀 aa6 contractions, 二百/兩百, 2,362 and colloquial 一萬二 against the same article; 四十四 sei3 a6 sei3 and entering-tone numbering against the Jyutping article; 圓/元, 蚊, 毫, 仙 and the HK$7.80 / 6.75 / 7.08 patterns against the Hong Kong dollar article (Yale-to-Jyutping conversion checked); Wiktionary 蚊 man4-1 money classifier, 個 go3 money classifier, 兩 loeng5. Changed: the 兩隻豬 example was attributed to Wiktionary's 兩 entry but is in the 隻 entry, so re-attributed and added 隻 and 蚊 Wiktionary sources; replaced the unsourced 'a million is 一百萬' framing with arithmetic (100,000 = 10 x 10,000) and cut an unsourced claim that Thai and Khmer share the ten-thousand grouping; 仙 'survives mainly' changed to 'used only' in the stock market per source; FAQ no longer says two is always ji6 inside longer numbers (Wikipedia accepts 兩百). App claims (12 units, numbers/money/dates, characters with Jyutping, tone contrasts, ads plus optional IAP) match the catalog.

Fetched all three cited Gboard help pages (saved sources/x_gb1, x_gb2, x_gb3): keyboard and Settings-app routes, layout and Done steps, device language unaffected, Android 7.0 note, Android 8 Go edition warning, Open features menu > More > Settings, space-bar and language-switch-key methods incl. the greyed-out tip, troubleshooting order (restart, update, clear cache/data, force stop), Personalization and text correction, 'stick to one or two active languages'; the supported-language list confirms Vietnamese, Thai, Khmer, Khmer Surin, Lao, Lao Transliteration, five Malay Brunei/Malaysia/Singapore entries, Chinese Cantonese Traditional and Burmese. Gboard Jyutping support checked against Wikipedia Jyutping. Recomputed 5 Malay entries and 2 + 5 = 7. Changed: 'your menus stay in English' to device menus keep their current language; replaced the unsourced 'makes switching quicker' claim with arithmetic tied to Google's one-or-two advice; accessed dates updated to 2026-10-25 after re-opening. App mentions (Learn Vietnamese Language Fast dictation, sentence building, tones; the other four courses exist) match catalog. Distinct from khmer-fonts-on-android (input vs display).

Verified against saved Comprehensible output text (Swain; noticing, hypothesis-testing with interlocutor feedback, metalinguistic functions; Krashen's 'output is rare' criticism and preference for more comprehensible input; speaking at the top of students' anxiety list; pushing students to speak may hamper acquisition), Private speech text (definition, audible but not directed at others, Vygotsky and Piaget, young-adult self-report questionnaire) and the two PubMed abstracts (Jiang et al. 2025: 64 Chinese-speaking L2 English learners, picture-description task, private speech facilitates L2 oral production, 32 users in the fNIRS experiment, proficiency-dependent role; Takeuchi et al. 2021: 4-week shadowing and reading-aloud training, tendency towards greater digit-span increases and significantly greater n-back reaction-time decreases). Speech shadowing text: a technique to practise speech, tasks of incremental difficulty. Changed: the Takeuchi comparison groups were 'training groups without speaking' (compressed-speech listening and an active L2 control), not 'groups who only listened'; corrected in body, FAQ and takeaway. Cut the claim that the shadowing article warns errors become habits (not in the source). Session arithmetic 4+6+6+4=20 and 20x5=100 checked. Distinct from shadowing-technique-explained and learning-a-language-without-a-teacher. App claims (audio, pronunciation practice, dictation, roleplay, not a substitute for conversation) match catalog.

Verified against saved Italian conjugation text (x_itconj: 'all transitive verbs and most intransitive verbs' take avere; 'small number of intransitive verbs' with essere incl. venire/andare/arrivare; avere/arrivare paradigms; l'ho vista; reflexives mi sono lavato/-a, ci siamo visti), Italian grammar wikitext (passive Il cancello è stato appena aperto; 'a reliable rule cannot be given'; vivere ho/sono vissuto; egli è partito/ella è partita; l'ho mangiata; optional agreement non mi ha chiamato/a; stato shared with stare; leggere -> letto) and Unaccusative verb text (È arrivato vs Ha telefonato; be/have split; variation by meaning/region). Worked example re-derived (3 essere, 2 avere). Changed: the 'Where the rule runs out' sentence misread the citation-needed tag, which sits on the reflexive/unaccusative sentence, not on the rule of thumb (that one cites the Accademia della Crusca); rewrote to match the wikitext. Distinct from passato-prossimo-vs-imperfetto (tense choice) and italian-verb-conjugation-basics (present tense). App claims (verbs, agreement, common tenses, past-events unit) match catalog.

Verified against Ciao article (hello and goodbye; mainly informal, with those addressed as tu; s-ciào vostro '(I am) your slave'; shortened and lost servile connotations; adopted in northern Italy late 19th/early 20th c.), Italian grammar wikitext (tu/Lei since the Renaissance, Sie/vous, Lei takes third-person forms, Lei è alto, voi formal in Campania, formal Loro very rarely used) and T-V wikitext (dare del tu / dare del Lei); Wiktionary log for buongiorno (good day/morning, good afternoon only very early afternoon, syn buon pomeriggio), buondì (colloquial), buonasera usage note (~5pm, far south), salve (syn ciao/buongiorno/buonasera; 'too stiff even for formal occasions'), arrivederla (formal, Lei; ci vediamo informal), come stai/come sta, piacere. Changed: table row now says buongiorno covers the 'very early afternoon' per Wiktionary, and the 15:30 worked step now uses buon pomeriggio (the 5pm line divides pomeriggio from sera, not buongiorno from buonasera). Arithmetic 19-17=2 checked. App claims (greetings in core path, culture and etiquette, roleplay) match catalog.

Verified every cardinal 0-99, the 100 to 1,000,000,000 rows, 101 centouno/centuno, 108 centootto/centotto, 180 centottanta, ordinals primo-decimo and -esimo forms incl. ventitreesimo, the -tré rule, mille/mila, milione/miliardo + di (miliardi di lire), due mila variant, 25.000 thousands separator, 860.789 split, 3,5 tre virgola cinque, più/meno/per/diviso, cento e una pagina, il trenta di maggio against the saved Wiktionary Appendix:Italian numbers text. Lira/euro dates (unit of account 1999, cash 2002) and 100 cents checked against saved Italian lira and Euro pages. Recomputed 860x1000+789=860,789 and 1000+900+84=1984. Changed: cut the unsourced 'about thirty pieces' estimate; il Trecento now glossed as 1301-1400, the 14th century, as the source states (was 'the 1300s'). App claims (numbers unit, audio, dictation) match catalog.

Verified against Italian grammar wikitext: general endings table (cappello nero, bella macchina, comandante, atleta, specie, città, manager), -io -> -i (esempio, funzionario), invariables (gru, città, caffè, film), -co/-go rules of thumb with the Serianni quote, funghi/fuochi/medici/comici, the -logo split, exceptions amico/greco/valico, -ca/-ga, -cia/-gia rule and farmacia, poeta/poeti, cane/parete, masculine-singular/feminine-plural nouns (uovo, braccio, ginocchio, dito), braccia/bracci and corna/corni meaning split, irregulars uomo, dio/dei with gli, bue, tempio (mostly from Vulgar Latin). Orthography wikitext confirms camicia/valigia/provincia and 'established since the 1950s'. Worked five-noun example re-derived (1 invariable, 4 change). No changes needed. App claims (articles, agreement, 12 units) match catalog.

Verified against Italian grammar wikitext: closed class; tra/fra interchangeable by euphony (tra fratelli, fra i tralicci); mandatory contraction of di/a/da/in/su and the full 35-cell table (5x7 recomputed); optional con/per forms archaic except col/coi; article-less phrases a capo, da capo, di colpo, in bicicletta, per strada; su di before pronouns, and before u 'regarded as incorrect by grammarians'. Wiktionary texts (x_it_di, x_it_da, x_it_in, x_it_su) confirm every quoted example: coda del cane, Monreale, più alto di sua moglie, dell'acqua, ira di Apollo, Divina Commedia, libri di matematica, collana d'oro, dalla terra alla luna, da Giovanni, dal dottore, da quando, dai ladri, macchina da scrivere, libro da leggere, panetteria, in autobus, sulla tavola. Changed: the su proportion example 'uno su cinque' is not in the source; replaced with Wiktionary's own 'un europeo su cinque', 'one European in five'. App claims match catalog.

Verified against Italian orthography and phonology wikitext: 'almost completely phonemic' and its listed exceptions; 21 letters (5 vowels, 16 consonants), j/k/w/x/y in loanwords, names and scientific terms (weekend, jeans, km); open/closed e and o only in stressed syllables, closed only when unstressed; accents generally found only in dictionaries, pèsca/pésca limited to didactic texts; glides with exceptions fatuo, viaggio; hard/soft c and g table (china, Cina, caramella, ciaramella, ghiro, giro, gallo, giallo); camicia vs farmacia; sc/sci/sch (scerno, scialo, scherno); gli/gn long between vowels (aglio, ogni); silent h (ho/o etc.); s rules (Sara, sbranare, always voiced in the north); z (canzone, zanzara); r trill with one or two contacts / tap; fato/fatto and the minimal pairs; syntactic gemination triggers and a casa, central/southern use vs inconsistent northern use; lexical stress with penult preferred; accent compulsory only on a final stressed vowel (sanità, perché, morì); IPA of occhi, giallo, aglio, zoccolo, canzone, passato. 21+5=26 and giallo six letters / five sounds checked. No changes needed. App claims (audio, dictation, pronunciation practice) match catalog.

Verified Wiktionary texts: vorrei (first-person conditional of volere; polite requests), per favore/per piacere, prenotazione, tavolo, frizzante, cameriere/cameriera, conto (calculation; bank account; bill for a meal, hotel), scusi (formal second-person singular, see also scusa), coperto (cover, cover charge, place at dining table). Italian cuisine wikitext: course table (aperitivo examples, antipasto, primo most frequent, secondo, contorno with salad alongside the main course, formaggio e frutta, dolce, caffè, digestivo), full-course meals mainly for special events, food-establishment descriptions (trattoria, osteria, ristorante, pizzeria, tavola calda). Cover charge page: pane e coperto nearly ubiquitous in Italy; Lazio 1995, EU ruling 1998. Worked bill recomputed: 22+16+5+3+5 = 51, order before coperto 46. Changed: cut 'most regions serve bread at the table', which the saved cuisine text does not say. Prices are labelled as invented for illustration. App claims (food unit, restaurant travel material, audio) match catalog.

Fetched lshk.org/jyutping-scheme (saved sources/x_lshk.txt): 1993 design, alphanumeric without diacritics, null initial 呀 = aa, fu1-fu6 examples, 2018 addition of a and oet, ASCII-digit tone numbers and acceptance of bold/italic/colour all confirmed. Wikipedia Jyutping wikitext confirms the initials table with IPA and example characters (渣, 叉, 也, 牙, 瓜, 誇), finals examples (三, 心, 鋸, 商, 詢, 需, 書), syllabic m/ng 唔 吳, nine tones in six contours with entering tones written 1/3/6 (識 sik1, 錫 sek3, 食 sik6), ILE 1-9, the name contraction, the z/c and y-to-j innovation, j before bare yu, the Yale differences, the gwong2 zau1 waa2 / jyut6 jyu5 / nei5 hou2 examples and Gboard. Recomputed 2 + 2 + 3 = 7. No changes needed. Distinct from cantonese-tones-explained (reads the spelling, defers tone sounds). App claims match catalog.

Verified against saved Khmer script wikitext: 35 symbols/33 used, ឝ ឞ obsolete, inherent â/ô, voiceless/voiced origin and Middle Khmer sound changes, ណ adapted as a-series counterpart of ន, ឋ ឌ ឍ rare, ប [ɓ]/[p], subscripts (none for ឡ, cheung âksâr), dominance rule and ត្រា example, musĕkâtônd (ង ញ ម យ រ វ; ប to p), treisăpt (ស ហ ប អ), kbiĕs kraôm, supplementary consonants under ហ, final ដ/ឌ [t], k-letters glottal after [aː]/[iə], រ silent, ស [h], one final consonant. Series table recounted with node (15 + 18 = 33). Wiktionary ក (neck) and គ (mute; deaf) confirmed. No changes needed; app claims match catalog.

All Khmer words, digits and UNGEGN forms match saved Khmer numerals wikitext; verified biquinary description, proto-Austroasiatic 1-5, Sanskrit zero, reduced mə, pəm in 6-9, colloquial dândáb teens (15 = ប្រាំដណ្ដប់), mphey contraction, 30-90 borrowed from southern Middle Chinese via Thai and not decomposable, informal 81 pêt muŏy, Thai-origin rôy/poăn/mœn/sên/léan and Sanskrit/Pali kaôdĕ with its billion ambiguity and dáb léan, dáb poăn alternative, ordinals with ទី compared to Thai thi and Vietnamese thứ, digits since the early 7th century and earliest zero evidence. Riel infobox and text confirm banknotes, rare coins, dollar use and the 4,000-riel retail rate with riel change; Wiktionary ប៉ុន្មាន confirms 'how much?, how many?' and the time example. Recomputed 27, 36, 4,100, 15,000 and 2.50 x 4,000 = 10,000. App claims (script, numbers, currency, market bargaining, ads + optional IAP) match catalog. No net changes.

Dependent vowel table checked row by row against the saved Khmer script wikitext (both series IPA and UNGEGN for all 16 signs, Battambang-based values, dialect variation), plus srăk nĭssăy/phsâm, pronounced after the consonant, nĭkkôhĕt/reăhmŭkh combinations (អុំ អំ អាំ អះ values, ធំ [tʰom]/[tʰum]), bânták effects, yŭkôlpĭntŭ, independent vowels (sră pénh tuŏ, glottal/liquid, mostly Indic, ឥឡូវ ឪពុក ឬ ឮ glosses) and the លា léa [liə] and ត្រា examples. Khmer language wikitext confirms the *kaa/*gaa breathy-voice history ending in [kaː]/[kiə] and that written words never begin with a regular vowel. App claims (vowels with pronunciation help, romanised spelling, tracing, slowed audio) match catalog. No changes needed.

Vowel table checked row by row against saved Lao script wikitext (final/medial forms, IPA, BGN/PCGN), special vowels with old alternatives, Luang Prabang [aɰ] and Houaphanh [ɯ] notes, silent ອ base, sala naming and named marks, 1975 spelling reform, ◌ະ glottal stop. Lao language wikitext confirms all vowels make a length distinction, a short vowel must be followed by a coda, ʔ only after a short vowel, ຫັກ/ຮັກ/ຫາກ/ຮາກ with tones and glosses, four tones before p/t/k and two before ʔ. App claims (script first, character recognition, sounds, reading words, free with ads, no IAP) match catalog. Fixed: short diphthong and ɤ IPA now carry the glottal stop as in the source (iaʔ, ɯaʔ, uaʔ, ɤʔ) so short and long no longer look identical; heading now uses the source's ◌ໍາ/ເ◌ົາ forms; corrected the description of the Lao tone rules article, which lists four inputs, not three.

Wiktionary: Isnin (Arabic, alt Senin, syn Hari Satu), Selasa, Rabu (Classical Malay from an Arabic form), Khamis (alt Kamis), Jumaat, Sabtu, Ahad (syn Minggu), minggu 'week' from Portuguese domingo, the month template list, Januari/Ogos from English, Mac/Ogos vs Indonesian Maret/Agustus, bulan moon/month with example, pukul (hit; hour; pukul tiga), jam, setengah (se- + tengah), suku (Sekarang satu suku), pagi, petang (syn sore), malam (Selamat malam), tengah hari. Wikipedia comparison: Sunday Ahad vs Minggu/Ahad, pukul tujuh setengah = 7.30 vs Indonesian setengah tujuh = 6.30 from Dutch half zeven, Malaysia 12-hour standard vs Indonesia/Brunei/Singapore 24-hour. Day-names article: Arabic al-ithnayn/al-khamis and the 'gather' and 'Sabbath' notes for Jumaat and Sabtu. Arithmetic 7+0.5 and 7-0.5 checked. No edits needed.

Wiktionary entries checked: belas (combining word 11-19, lapan belas tahun example), puluh (Kedukan Bukit 683 CE, sapulu/sepuluh), ratus and ribu (inherited; seribu current spelling), sebelas (se- + belas, alt satu belas), sifar (formal, from Arabic, syn kosong informal, Indonesian nol), kosong ('empty'), berapa (amount/value/time/measurement, pukul berapa, umur berapa). Wikipedia comparison of Indonesian and Standard Malay: 1,234,567.89 read with perpuluhan lapan vs 1.234.567,89 with koma delapan. Malaysian ringgit wikitext: banknotes and 5-50 sen coins in frequent use, 1 sen discontinued but legal tender, rounding of the total bill to the nearest 5 sen since 1 April 2008, kupang in Kedah/northern Peninsula. Recomputed RM12.43 -> 12.45 and RM12.42 -> 12.40 with node. Changed: 'one is usually the prefix se-' (unsourced 'usually') to 'can be'.

Common-pronoun table, saya/aku usage, kami/kita (confused in colloquial Indonesian but not Malay), sa(ha)ya sekalian, beta/patik, anda/kamu/kalian, engkau/kau, awak, encik/cik, ia/dia (ia recently used for animals), beliau, baginda, mereka vs dia orang, possessive enclitics -ku/-mu/-kau/-nya with the meja examples, proclitics ku-/kau-, and the shop assistant's 'Boleh dibantu?' all checked against Wikipedia Malay grammar wikitext; korang/kitorang/diorang against Malaysian Malay. Changed: cut the unsourced generalisation 'many speakers avoid a second-person pronoun' to a neutral lead-in to Wikipedia's statement.

All table examples and glosses checked against Wiktionary entries for apa (apakah formal interrogative; derived siapa/berapa/mengapa/apabila; bare Apa? often considered impolite, Maaf? preferred), siapa (who/whose; Siapa nama kamu?), mana (incomplete without di/ke/dari; 'which' with optional yang; macam mana), di mana and yang mana (relative use proscribed by DBP), bila (conjunction use proscribed, apabila prescribed), mengapa (syn kenapa, apa hal, apa pasal), kenapa (informal; mengapa formal), bagaimana, berapa and -kah (modal verbs/adverbs in questions; emphasis on question words; examples). Wikipedia Malay grammar: focused element first, followed by a slight pause. Added Wiktionary's usage note that -kah is usually only used in formal or literary speech or writing.

Checked against Wikipedia Marathi grammar wikitext: shabdayogi avyaya = preposition; saamaanya ruup with घोडा -> घोड्यावर; the two-case direct/oblique analysis with rām-ā-lā and the oblique suffix depending on gender and final vowel; the eight vibhakti suffixes and every example sentence (घराला रंग दिला, लेखणीने, मुलाला ओळखतो, गावाहून, घराचा दरवाजा, घरात, मुलांनो शांत बसा); -hūna after vowels and -ūna on the direct form (घरून); -त vs -ई connotation (well-defined area vs less well-defined place, gharāt/gharī) and obligatory सकाळी; differential object marking dagaḍa/dagaḍālā; ergative मुलाने पुरी खाल्ली; genitive agreeing with the governing noun; Wiktionary मी for माझ्यासाठी. 7 + 1 = 8 checked. No edits needed.

Fetched Wiktionary for तू, तुम्ही, आपण, आम्ही, मी, तो and तुला: formality ranking and grammatical number, आपण as inclusive we and polite you with both examples, आम्ही exclusive, तो distal with both examples and हा/ही/हे, मी declension (मला, माझ्याने/माझ्याशी, ablative, माझ्यासाठी, माझ्यात, alt मज/माझ्यास), तुला acc/dat of तू. Wikipedia Marathi grammar: pronoun table glosses (formal, extremely formal), gender on verbs not pronouns in 1st/2nd person, demonstrative table, possessive table and agreement with the modified noun; दरवाजा/तब्येत/पत्रक genders from its case examples; 6 x 3 = 18 recomputed. Changed: an FAQ called मज/माझ्यास 'more formal or written' (unsourced) - now 'alternative forms'; added the Wiktionary तुला entry to sources (accessed 2026-10-25), since तुला is not given in the तू entry.

Verified the 45/10/45 regions, Hanoi-based standard, 1954 migration figures (about a million south, 150,000 north), d/gi/r, ch-tr, s-x and v correspondences, vocabulary rows (vâng/dạ, thìa/muỗng, bát/chén, ô tô/xe hơi, dĩa/nĩa, đĩa/dĩa, này/nè, đấy/đó), dạ vâng mixing and ông ấy -> ổng / bà ấy -> bả against Vietnamese language wikitext; HCMC final merger, qu-/hu-/u- -> [w] and the hỏi-ngã merger against Vietnamese phonology; nghìn/ngàn and 101 against Vietnamese numerals; muỗng/thìa against Wiktionary. Changed: '45% of speakers' (source gives only percentages) to plain percentages; 'all mutually intelligible' now carries Wikipedia's caveat that North-Central/Central varieties are less intelligible; cut a lip-rounding claim presented as southern (source describes it generally); 'rice bowl' to 'bowl'; removed unsourced 'learners often ask', 'r varies by speaker' and 'many materials follow Hanoi ... neither is more correct'. App claims match catalog.

Verified against Italian conjugation text: present perfect for single actions/events and change of state, with all four examples (stamattina sono andato a scuola, si è arrabbiato..., andavo in bicicletta..., si arrabbiava...); three imperfect uses incl. weather, time, age; sapevo/ho saputo la verità; imperfect formation stem + thematic vowel + v + endings; essere the only irregular imperfect; dicevo, facevo, bevevo. Italian grammar wikitext glosses facevo as 'I used to do / I was doing'. Imperfect article: stavo parlando and 'I eat' vs 'I am eating'. Preterite article: passato remoto for an action completed far in the past; colloquial use increases north to south; Northern Italians and Sardinians use the passato prossimo in any perfective situation. Worked story re-derived (3 imperfetti + 2 passati prossimi = 5; arrivare and uscire take essere, usciti agrees). No changes needed. Distinct from italian-essere-vs-avere (auxiliary choice). App claims (common tenses, past-events unit) match catalog.

Hard-stem новый, soft-stem синий, высокий, хороший and большой tables checked against Wikipedia Russian declension wikitext; rules (и after sibilant/velar, stressed -ой, хорошее rule, animacy accusative, -ою variant, -ого/-его read -ово/-ево) all match; short forms нов/нова/ново/новы only in the nominative and predicative (Russian grammar); relational adjectives unlikely to have short forms.
